name: The Holocaust: Persecution, Murder and Memory
description: How Nazi Germany moved from laws against Jews to the murder of six million, who resisted and who rescued, and how the world judged and remembered the crime.

checkpoints.name: A republic falls
checkpoints.note: The Weimar Republic is born from defeat in 1918 and shaken by crisis. Adolf Hitler builds the Nazi Party into a mass movement, and in Mein Kampf he sets out a world view in which Jews are cast as Germany's enemy.

checkpoints.name: Persecution
checkpoints.note: Hitler takes power in 1933 and Nazi Germany becomes a dictatorship, with Heinrich Himmler's SS running the camps. The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 strip Jews of citizenship, and the violence of Kristallnacht in 1938 prompts the Kindertransport, which carries children to safety in Britain.

checkpoints.name: War and the ghettos
checkpoints.note: Germany invades Poland and starts World War II. Polish Jews are forced into ghettos, the largest in Warsaw, and Auschwitz opens as a camp. After Operation Barbarossa in 1941, killing squads shoot Jews in the east, more than thirty thousand at Babi Yar in two days.

checkpoints.name: The death camps
checkpoints.note: At the Wannsee Conference officials plan the deportation of all Europe's Jews. Treblinka and Auschwitz become sites of mass murder, and the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising fights back in 1943. Anne Frank's family is discovered in hiding in 1944, while Oskar Schindler and Raoul Wallenberg save thousands.

checkpoints.name: Judgement and memory
checkpoints.note: The camps are freed in 1945, after the Holocaust has killed some six million Jews; Primo Levi and Elie Wiesel survive to bear witness. The Nuremberg trials judge Nazi leaders, Anne Frank's diary appears, Israel and Yad Vashem are founded, Eichmann is tried, and Maus and Schindler's List carry the story on.
